items.question: Which practice best demonstrates the concept of sustainable forestry?

choices.A: Harvesting all mature trees at once
choices.C: Burning forests to improve soil fertility

items.explanation: Sustainable forestry involves managing forests to meet current needs without compromising future use; replanting and selective logging ensure the forest can regenerate.

rationalization.why_A: Clear-cutting all mature trees can lead to erosion and habitat loss, often making it unsustainable.
rationalization.why_B: Replanting after selective logging is the correct answer; it maintains the forest ecosystem while still providing timber.
rationalization.why_C: Burning forests (slash-and-burn) provides temporary fertility but is highly destructive and unsustainable.
rationalization.why_D: Converting forests to farms is deforestation, the opposite of sustainable forestry.
